name: Toybox Pixel for Snap and Spell

extends.name: Toybox Pixel
extends.note: The Snake tokens are used unchanged. This file lists what Snap and Spell uses from them, and adds only what the game needs.

shared.note: Snake tokens that Snap and Spell uses as they are. Values are in tokens.json and are not repeated here.
typography: phone type roles as the starting scale
notUsed: medalGold|Silver|Bronze (a leaderboard does not exist here)
tongue and eye as snake parts (the pink and white stay as palette colours)
scoreFormat six digits is kept for points

jewel.note: Five gem colours, all from the shared palette. A gem's colour is decoration. Its shape and size say its tier, so no rule depends on 'the red one'.
jewel.shade: ink at 28 percent, bottom-right cells (the same bevel as segmentBevel)

die.note: A die is the same in every theme: it is the physical toy on the table.

tray.wellPattern: checkerboard, one cell behind each die

surfaceDim.use: Disabled fills and the empty well of a panel
surfaceDim.note: new, a darker cream; text on it is ink at full strength, never faded

path.note: Stepped (square caps), so it stays crisp at integer scale

night.note: Toybox Night, the dark scheme. Snake has no dark scheme; Snap and Spell keeps its existing Colour scheme setting (light, dark, system), so a night set is defined from the same palette.

shadowDeep.note: new: the hard shadow must be darker than the page

tileState.note: Every state differs in shape or position as well as colour (WCAG 1.4.1). Letters are ink on every state fill; the ratios are in contrast.

pressed.mark: the die sinks 3px while a finger or key is down

inPath.mark: order badge (1, 2, 3 ...) in a 24px ink disc at the top-left corner

start.mark: the start-tile help: a dashed ring and a small play triangle at the top-left

hint.mark: a second letter's tile in the two-letter help: sunshine fill and a dot at the top-left

valid.mark: check pip (ink on cream disc) at the top-right, held for 600 ms, then the tiles settle

invalid.mark: x pip (white on ink disc) at the top-right and a two-step sideways shake (omitted with reduced motion)
invalid.note: ink text on pink is 4.16:1, below 4.5, so pink is an outline only

doubtful.mark: a question-mark pip (ink on sunshine disc) at the top-right: used on the scan check screen

disabled.note: not faded; ink text keeps full contrast

selectedChoice.mark: check glyph before the label, outline 4px

focus.ring: 4px dashed ink, 3px gap; on Night: surface
focus.note: visible on every control after a key press

danger.note: a pink fill would put text on pink (4.16:1); the outline and the glyph carry the warning

typography.note: Toybox type is for the chrome. The dice, the words a child reads and every numeral stay in Andika (SIL OFL, already bundled). Pixelify Sans has an O and a 0 that match, a G that reads as 6, and a and g that read as blobs (screenshots/_legibility.png); at 16 to 30 px its 2, 3 and 5 read as Z, 8 and S (125 % looks like 128 %, 5 words like S words), and Silkscreen's digits have the same fault in a smaller degree.

reading.use: dice letters, found words, sentences a child or parent reads

counter.use: upper-case labels (eyebrows) at 16 px and above. Never digits.

points.format: six digits, zero padded, for totals; +13 for a word; tabular figures

textScale.note: the parent's Text size setting, kept

candidates: Noto Sans SC and Noto Sans JP (SIL OFL), subset to the glyphs of the catalogues
Fusion Pixel Font zh-Hans and ja (SIL OFL 1.1), checked per file before it ships
rejected: Zpix: paid licence for commercial use, modification forbidden

rtl.note: Pixelify Sans has no Hebrew; Yiddish uses the same face

pixelUnit.rule: Outlines (3, 4, 6 px), hard shadows (3, 4, 6, 12 px) and pixel art are drawn in whole device pixels. On a display with a fractional scale factor they are rounded to the nearest whole device pixel, never blurred.
pixelUnit.note: Snake letterboxes and scales its whole board in integer steps. Here the layout is fluid (eight languages, a parent text size, windows from 900 x 620), so only the borders, shadows and sprites are snapped, and the board scales in whole tile steps.

tray.frame: 6px ink outline plus 12px hard drop, as board.frame in tokens.json

gem.grid: 9 to 13 cells square, one cell = 3 device-independent px at the list size, 4 at the summary size

progress.segment: 12 x 20 with 3px gap, filled = accent, empty = surfaceDim
progress.note: used by the gate's hold button and nothing else

touch.note: Snap and Spell is played by five- and six-year-olds. The Snake floor of 44 px is the lowest value anywhere; the project's own, higher values stay.

shared: scorePop: a found word's +points rises 14 px over 1.6 s
reducedMotion: all looping animation, screen shake and flashing switch off

boxShake.note: the closed box jumps left and right by 6 px in 8 steps; reduced: the box stays still and the lid cross-fades

diceDrop.note: each die steps through six frames (a flip-book of pixel faces), staggered by 40 ms; reduced: the dice appear at once

gemBob.note: the shared foodBob, used on the summary's gems; reduced: still

tileFlash.note: valid and invalid marks; at most 3 flashes a second

motion.limits: Nothing loops for more than 5 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2); no screen shake for anyone; confetti stays within the board and the panel and is off with reduced motion.

contrast.method: WCAG 2.x relative luminance, computed from the hex values above (source/contrast.py).

pairs.use: all text on panels and dice
text on the page, start and hint tiles
primary button text, night text on panels
night: selected edge on a panel (non-text 3:1)

forbidden.rule: coral on sunshine has no edge of its own: a coral object on the page always has an ink outline

gemTierRule: The tier of a word (1, 2 or 5 stars by length) picks the shape. The colour is assigned in turn from the five values, so two found words of one tier may differ in colour. Nothing in the game, the help or the parent area refers to a gem by colour.
